children: G5 Entertainment proposes a voluntary redemption program of up to SEK 84.3M, paying SEK 80 per share, approximately 10% above the 10-day VWAP before the board’s November 26 resolution. Shareholders will vote on December 22, 2026.
Proposes redemption program of up to SEK 84.3M
Returns capital to shareholders; this is a proposal requiring shareholder approval, not a completed payout.
SEK 80 per share, about 10% above 10-day VWAP
The premium may support the share price, though it applies only to shares tendered and accepted under the program.
Seven redemption rights redeem one ordinary share
Sets the participation ratio and may influence trading in the rights and ordinary shares.
Up to 1,053,892 ordinary shares to be redeemed
Would reduce shares outstanding if fully completed; the proposal is subject to approval and take-up.
Shareholders vote on the proposal December 22, 2026
Approval is a key near-term condition; the board requires at least two-thirds of votes cast and shares represented.

This is a proposed capital return following the company’s stated 2026 cost savings and profitability, rather than a completed transaction. Shareholder approval on December 22 and the subsequent redemption-rights timetable will determine whether and to what extent the program proceeds.
